title: Business Valuation in Tampa
description: Frequently Asked Questions What is a business valuation and why do I need one? A business valuation is a formal analysis of what your company is worth based on its financials, market position, and risk profile. Owners need one before selling, during a partnership dispute, when applying for financing, or when building a long-term exit strategy. Without a defensible number built from your actual data, you are either leaving money on the table or pricing yourself out of a sale entirely. What is the difference between a business valuation and a broker's opinion of value? A broker's opinion of value is typically a quick estimate based on revenue multiples and comparable sales. A valuation built on formal appraisal methodology goes significantly deeper, analyzing recast earnings, customer concentration, owner dependency, recurring revenue, and the specific risk factors a sophisticated buyer will use to justify a lower offer. Tom holds a state appraisal certification and applies that same discipline to every opinion of value he delivers through TAMBAY Mergers & Acquisitions. How long does a business valuation take? Most valuations through TAMBAY are completed within two to three weeks from the time all financial documentation is received. The timeline depends on the complexity of your financials and how organized your records are going in. Tom reviews everything personally, so the process moves at the pace your documentation allows. What financial documents do I need for a valuation? At minimum you will need three years of profit and loss statements, three years of business tax returns, a current year-to-date profit and loss statement, and a balance sheet. Additional documents such as equipment lists, customer concentration data, and lease agreements help build a more complete picture. description: SUPPORTING THE FULL LIFECYCLE OF THE DEAL The quality of what happens upstream determines the quality of what is possible downstream. A deal does not start when a seller calls. It starts with whether the seller called you or someone else. And why. How that moment is set up determines the quality of everything that follows: the listing conversation, the buyer process, the close, and the next referral. BEFORE THE DEAL Getting sellers to call you before they call anyone else The quality of the listing conversation is determined before it starts. A broker with the right system does not compete for attention. They create the conditions under which the right sellers find them first, already convinced. By the time a seller reaches out, the competition has already been removed from the equation. Lead Capture Seller Nurture Sequences Education Funnels Lead Source Tracking THE LISTING CONVERSATION Walking in with the work already done When the upstream work is done correctly, the listing conversation is not an interview. The broker is assessing fit. The seller is confirming that what they encountered before the conversation is true in the room. The process, the valuation education, the onboarding approach... all of it has already made the case. Seller Onboarding Valuation Education Virtual Data Room Marketing Material INSIDE THE DEAL A system that moves deals forward without pulling the broker into every step The broker's attention goes where it actually changes the outcome. That is only possible when the system has handled everything that does not require the broker's judgment. A buyer who has reviewed the CIM, watched the seller interview, signed the NDA, and submitted questions before the first call is an entirely different buyer.
